page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7se.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average single-core performance but weaker multi-core scaling. The stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both fall into the average tier, while multi-core metrics, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, are categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth tests, such as large-block read and write operations, also show weak performance, though Passmark memory scores and single-threaded decompression tasks like bzip3 maintain average ratings.

From a resource density perspective, the ecs.r7se.xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-bound applications that do not require intensive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the lower multi-core compute efficiency and weak database operation performance, as seen in the Passmark database and Redis SET benchmarks. Because there is no bundled local storage, users must factor in the performance of external block storage.

This instance is suited for memory-intensive, low-compute workloads. Appropriate use cases include small-scale in-memory caching, lightweight database hosting, text processing, and single-threaded application servers where memory capacity is prioritized over raw multi-threaded CPU throughput.
